projects.name: FlowDesk
projects.tagline: Project & sprint management for product teams
projects.summary: ExplainerAI explored 37 pages of FlowDesk, isolated five workflows that carry the product's core value, and narrated the top-ranked path end to end. Every claim in the script is anchored to a DOM element captured during exploration.

workflows.title: Create Project → Add Tasks → Assign Owner
workflows.description: The canonical first-run path: a new user lands on an empty workspace, spins up their first project, fills it with tasks and hands ownership to a teammate.

steps.action: Click the "New Project" button on the dashboard
Type a project name and pick a workspace colour
steps.element: Text input "Project name" inside Create Project modal

steps.action: Confirm creation and land on the empty project board
Add three tasks inline from the To-do column
Open a task and assign it to a teammate from the owner picker

workflows.title: Invite Teammate → Set Role Permissions
workflows.description: Admin path covering seat invitation, role selection and the permission matrix that gates billing and workspace settings.

steps.action: Open workspace settings from the avatar menu
Move to the Members tab and click Invite people
Enter an email address and choose the Editor role
steps.element: Role select with options Viewer / Editor / Admin

steps.action: Send the invite and observe the pending state in the member list

workflows.title: Build a Sprint Board → Drag Tasks Across Columns
workflows.description: Demonstrates the drag-and-drop board, WIP limits and how status changes propagate to the sprint burndown in real time.

steps.action: Switch the project view from List to Board
Start a sprint from the board toolbar
Drag a task from To-do into In progress
Watch the burndown chart update in the sprint panel

workflows.title: Generate Weekly Progress Report → Export CSV
workflows.description: Reporting path that produces a shareable weekly digest and exports the underlying rows for finance and leadership review.

steps.action: Open Reports from the primary navigation
Select the Weekly progress template and set the date range
Click Export and choose CSV
steps.element: Export button on the Reports page

steps.action: Confirm the download toast appears

workflows.title: Connect Slack → Configure Notifications
workflows.description: Integration path showing the OAuth handshake and the per-event notification matrix that follows it.

steps.action: Open the Integrations directory from settings
Click Connect on the Slack card
Approve the OAuth scopes and return to ExplainerAI
Toggle notifications for task assignment and sprint close

parts.text: FlowDesk is where product teams turn a blank workspace into a shipping plan. You start on the dashboard and click
New Project
— name it, pick a colour, and you land straight on an empty board.
Tasks go in from the
inline composer
, so you never lose your place, and each one gets an owner from the
assignee picker
When the plan is ready, switch to the board and
start a sprint
. Dragging a card into In progress updates the
burndown chart
immediately — no status meeting required.
At the end of the week, the Reports tab builds the digest for you, and the
Export button

anchor.label: Export button on the Reports page

parts.text: hands finance the raw rows. That is FlowDesk — plan, ship, and prove it in one place.

projects.name: HelixPay
projects.tagline: Payments, subscriptions and payouts for modern commerce
projects.summary: A payments dashboard is dense with irreversible actions, so exploration ran in read-only mode. ExplainerAI ranked the payment-link flow highest: it is the shortest path from signup to first revenue.

workflows.title: Create Payment Link → Share with Customer
workflows.description: Fastest route to a first transaction: build a hosted checkout link, brand it, and copy it to the clipboard.

steps.action: Click "Create" and choose Payment link
Set a product name, amount and currency
Preview the hosted checkout page in the side panel
Copy the link and observe the confirmation toast

workflows.title: Set Up a Recurring Subscription Plan
workflows.description: Billing configuration covering interval, trial period and proration behaviour when a customer upgrades mid-cycle.

steps.action: Open Products and click New plan
Choose a monthly interval and add a 14-day trial
Enable prorated upgrades in advanced settings
Save the plan and see it appear in the pricing table

workflows.title: Reconcile Payout → Download Statement
workflows.description: Finance path that matches a bank payout to its underlying charges and refunds, then exports a signed statement.

steps.action: Open Balances → Payouts and select the latest payout
Expand the breakdown of charges, refunds and fees
Download the statement as PDF
Verify the reconciliation banner turns green

workflows.title: Add Team Member with Refund Permissions
workflows.description: Least-privilege admin flow: invite a support agent and grant refund rights without exposing payout settings.

steps.action: Open Settings → Team and click Invite member
Pick the Support role and tick Issue refunds
Send the invite and open the audit log entry

parts.text: HelixPay gets you to your first payment without touching a line of code. From the dashboard, hit
Create → Payment link
, set an amount, and a hosted checkout page is built for you.
The
live preview
shows exactly what your customer sees, and one click copies the link straight to your clipboard.
Recurring revenue works the same way: create a plan, choose an interval, and switch on
prorated upgrades
so mid-cycle changes bill themselves correctly.
And when money lands in your bank, the payout view reconciles every charge and fee, then hands you a
signed statement
your accountant will actually accept.

projects.name: NorthStar CRM
projects.tagline: Pipeline, sequences and lead scoring for revenue teams
projects.summary: NorthStar has a wide surface area, so ranking favoured workflows that chain three or more features together. The CSV import path won because it is both the first thing every team does and the one most often abandoned.

workflows.title: Import Leads from CSV → Map Fields
workflows.description: Bulk import with column mapping, duplicate detection and a dry-run preview before anything is written.

steps.action: Open Leads and click Import
Drop a CSV file into the upload zone
Map spreadsheet columns to CRM fields
steps.element: Mapping table with source → destination selects

steps.action: Review the dry-run summary and confirm the import

workflows.title: Build Deal Pipeline → Move Deal Stages
workflows.description: Configure a custom pipeline, then advance a deal through stages and watch the forecast recalculate.

steps.action: Open Pipelines and click Edit stages
Rename a stage and set its win probability
steps.element: Probability input inside the stage editor

steps.action: Drag a deal card into Negotiation
Confirm the forecast widget updates

workflows.title: Create Email Sequence → Schedule Follow-ups
workflows.description: Multi-step outreach with delays, branch-on-reply logic and a send-window guard for time zones.

steps.action: Open Sequences and click New sequence
Write the first email from a saved template
Add a three-day delay and a follow-up step
Set the send window and activate the sequence

workflows.title: Configure Lead Scoring Rules
workflows.description: Weighted scoring across firmographics and behaviour, with a live preview of how the current database re-ranks.

steps.action: Open Settings → Lead scoring
Add a rule that weights demo requests at +25
Check the live re-ranking preview panel

parts.text: NorthStar CRM begins where your data already lives. Open Leads, choose
Import
, and drop in a CSV. Columns are matched to fields automatically, and anything ambiguous is left for you to confirm.
Before a single record is written, a
dry-run summary
tells you what is new and what is a duplicate.
Deals move by dragging them between stages, and because each stage carries a win probability, the
weighted forecast
recalculates the moment you let go.
Follow-up is automated the same way — a sequence with delays, reply branching, and a
send window
that respects your prospect's local time.

projects.name: Quantly Analytics
projects.tagline: Product analytics with funnels and cohort retention
projects.summary: Exploration is still running. Three candidate workflows have been discovered so far; ranking will settle once the funnel builder has been traversed twice.

workflows.title: Build a Conversion Funnel → Compare Segments
workflows.description: Assemble a multi-step funnel from tracked events, then split it by acquisition channel to find the leak.

steps.action: Open Funnels and click New funnel
Add signup, activation and purchase as steps
Split the funnel by acquisition channel

workflows.title: Create a Retention Cohort → Export Chart
workflows.description: Weekly cohort grid with a rolling retention curve and a PNG export for the investor update.

steps.action: Open Retention and pick a weekly grain
Choose the activation event as the cohort anchor
Export the chart as PNG

workflows.title: Set an Alert on a Metric Threshold
workflows.description: Watch a metric and route a Slack alert when the seven-day average crosses a threshold.

steps.action: Open a saved metric and click Create alert
Set the threshold and the comparison window
Pick a Slack channel as the destination

projects.name: Shiftly HR
projects.tagline: Shift scheduling, time-off and payroll prep
projects.summary: The crawler has authenticated and is mapping the scheduling surface. Workflow candidates will appear here as they are discovered.

workflows.title: Publish a Weekly Schedule → Notify Staff
workflows.description: Draft a week of shifts from a template, resolve conflicts, and publish with an automatic notification to every assigned employee.

steps.action: Open the Schedule view for next week
Apply the "Standard week" template
Resolve the flagged double-booking
steps.element: Conflict badge on Thursday evening shift

steps.action: Publish the schedule and confirm notifications sent

projects.name: Vaultbase
projects.tagline: Managed Postgres with branching and point-in-time restore
projects.summary: A developer console with a small but deep surface. Ranking preferred workflows that demonstrate the branching model, which is Vaultbase's genuine differentiator.

workflows.title: Create a Database Branch → Run a Migration
workflows.description: Fork production into an isolated branch, apply a schema migration, and diff the result before merging.

steps.action: Click Branch on the production database card
Name the branch and confirm the copy-on-write notice
Run the pending migration from the console
Open the schema diff against production

workflows.title: Point-in-Time Restore to a New Branch
workflows.description: Pick a timestamp on the recovery timeline and materialise it as a fresh branch without touching production.

steps.action: Open the Backups tab and scrub the recovery timeline
Choose Restore to new branch
Watch the restore job stream its log lines

workflows.title: Rotate Connection Credentials
workflows.description: Generate a new role, rotate the connection string and confirm the old credential is revoked in the audit trail.

steps.action: Open Connection settings and click Rotate
Copy the new connection string
Confirm the revocation entry in the audit log

parts.text: Vaultbase treats your database the way you already treat your code. On the production card, press
Branch
, and a copy-on-write fork is ready in seconds.
Run your migration against the branch, then open the
schema diff
to see exactly what would change in production before anything ships.
If something does go wrong, scrub the
recovery timeline
to any second in the retention window and restore it as a new branch — production stays untouched.
